extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials responsible for standards policy (Standards Executives, agency leadership, NIST/OMB contacts, Interagency Committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting requirements for Federal agencies on participation in, adoption of, and management of voluntary consensus standards, and the charter/fuctions of the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy. Covers agency-level metrics, duties of Standards Executives, and interagency coordination mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of voluntary consensus standards as basis for mandatory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: As the basis for mandatory requirements, either by incorporating voluntary standards by reference, or including the normative portion of the standard in the FCC rules. Examples include ANSI measurement procedures, ANSI/ELA standards, EIA standards, ITU-R recommendations, EIA/TIA standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission can incorporate voluntary standards by reference or include normative portions in rules; this has been done for various technical areas. Where appropriate, agencies should look to voluntary industry standards instead of detailed regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defer detailed regulation when adequate voluntary standards exist
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has chosen not to implement regulations (or more detailed regulations) because adequate voluntary industry standards already exist or are under development (e.g., Personal Communications Service transmission protocol standards are not in regulation because industry developed them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When voluntary standards adequately address an area, agencies should prefer voluntary standards over prescriptive regulation and may allow industry-developed policies (e.g., 'spectrum etiquette') to establish practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of a voluntary consensus standard by agency
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may formally adopt a voluntary consensus standard (example: Commission adopted the DTV broadcast standard developed by ATSC on December 24, 1996).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and report official adoptions of voluntary consensus standards; adoption serves as an example of replacing separate regulatory development with consensus standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report number of voluntary consensus standards bodies and participating employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of voluntary consensus standards bodies in which there is agency participation, as well as the number of agency employees participating (e.g., 'NASA had 154 employees participating in 47 standards developing ... bodies').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must track and report both the count of standards bodies with agency participation and the personnel counts involved for OMB Circular A-119 reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report number of voluntary consensus standards used/adopted since reporting date
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has adopted/used since October 1, 1996 (or the applicable reporting period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should identify, count, and report standards that have been used or adopted in the reporting period; examples include standards 'incorporated by reference' or endorsed in regulatory guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify voluntary standards substituted for government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of voluntary consensus standards that have been substituted for government-unique standards as a result of an agency review of existing standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should undertake reviews of internal/government standards and identify and report cases where voluntary consensus standards replace government-unique documents (examples: NASA Centers canceling/superseding government documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate effectiveness of OMB Circular A-119 guidelines and recommend changes
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation of the effectiveness of the guidelines in the proposed revision to the Circular and recommendations for any changes (agencies provide an evaluation and recommendations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should analyze how proposed revisions affect their operations, recommend revisions if needed (e.g., NASA noted categorical reporting is useful and transaction reporting would be burdensome).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards Executive responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Standards Executive will carry out responsibilities by: (a) providing guidance to each of the agency's Commissioners on standards-related issues; (b) monitoring standards-setting activities of the agency's bureaus and offices and providing guidance on relation to OMB Circular A-119; (c) producing the reports required by OMB Circular A-119; (d) developing a five-year standards review cycle to be followed by each bureau/office to ensure compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a Standards Executive and ensure they perform these oversight, reporting, and planning functions to maintain compliance with OMB guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards Development Branch / office responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency office (e.g., Office of Engineering and Technology's Standards Development Branch) is tasked with coordinating standards activities within the agency and participating in/monitoring standards committees and national/international developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish or designate an organizational unit to monitor, participate in, and coordinate standards activities and to increase interaction with the private sector where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report when government-unique standards are used in lieu of voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by P.L. 104-113, agencies must report when government-unique standards are used in lieu of voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should record and report any instances where they choose government-unique standards over voluntary consensus standards and provide justification; many agencies report 'None' when they have not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards Management System and categorical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an agency-wide standards management system to support mission needs and as a basis for reporting use of voluntary consensus standards, replacement of government standards, etc.; use a 'categorical' (Standards Management System) based approach for reporting rather than burdensome transaction reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a standards management system that catalogs internal standards, identifies candidates for replacement, and supports agency-wide reporting and transition to voluntary consensus standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of internal standards for review and replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal government standards should be categorized (e.g., information technology, safety and mission assurance, engineering) to prioritize which standards are internal-only and which are candidates for substitution with voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on replacing government-unique engineering and other standards that have external applicability; retain internal-only standards for internal procedures or COTS preferences where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of lead center and policy documents for standards implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies implement OMB Circular A-119 through policy directives (e.g., NASA NPD 8070.6A) and may delegate authority to a Lead Center responsible for standardization support, program initiatives, procedures, and administering the Standards Management System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish and follow internal policy directives that define responsibilities, and delegate lead roles (e.g., a Lead Center) for operationalizing standards management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of voluntary standards in regulations and procurement documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should cite voluntary standards in regulations and procurement documents where possible (example: NARA citing voluntary standards in 36 CFR Chapter 12), and support staff participation on standards committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate voluntary consensus standards by reference in regulations/procurement to promote common methods and practices and support staff time/travel to participate in standards bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement of standards via regulatory guides (NRC example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory Guides (RGs) frequently endorse consensus standards; RGs describe acceptable methods for implementing regulations, are not substitutes for regulations, and compliance with them is not required; draft RGs are typically issued for 60-90 day public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, agencies may endorse standards through guidance documents (regulatory guides) and should follow public comment procedures for drafts; endorsement is a formal method to signal acceptable approaches without changing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency Committee purpose: ensure effective Federal participation and uniform policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee is established to advise on standards policy, ensure effective participation by the Federal Government in domestic and international standards activities, and promote adherence to uniform policies by Federal agencies in the development and use of standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Committee to coordinate Federal positions, promote consistency, and leverage standards to support competition, innovation, public safety, and environmental/metric goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee function: gather, analyze, and maintain standards-related information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee shall gather, analyze, and maintain current information about standards, product testing, quality system registration, accreditation, certification, and related regulations, rules, policies, and activities conducted by Federal agencies, private standards bodies, and regarding interagency/industry relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain up-to-date datasets and analyses of standards-related activities across agencies and with external organizations to inform policy and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee recommendations to Secretary of Commerce (policy objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the basis of information gathered, the Committee shall recommend actions to: (a) strengthen coordination among Federal agencies; (b) improve efficiency of standardization efforts with private sector and international bodies; (c) promote standards-related policies including directories of participating personnel; (d) ensure effective Federal representation at important meetings; (e) promote use of internationally acceptable standards to increase trade; (f) monitor U.S. technical obligations under treaties; (g) encourage agency strategic plans for managing voluntary standards; (h) promote standards serving national goals (metric system, environmentally sound and energy efficient practices); and (i) assess and improve adequacy of agency plans and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce actionable, targeted recommendations covering coordination, representation, strategic planning, international engagement, and alignment with national policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership requirements and designation of Standards Executive
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member agency's head shall ensure representation by a responsible high-level policy official (Senior Executive Service or higher) who serves as the agency representative on the Committee and also serves as the 'Standards Executive' as defined in OMB Circular A-119; alternates of equivalent status may be designated; appointments are for an indefinite term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require senior-level agency representation to the Committee, formal designation of Standards Executives, and allow designation of expert task-group members as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative provisions: chair, meetings, quorum, voting, and dissent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of NIST or designee shall chair the Committee; NIST provides administrative arrangements; the Committee shall meet at least three times each year; attendance by at least one half of designated members constitutes a quorum; internal decisions by majority of those present; recommendations to the Secretary require two-thirds of members present and voting; dissenting positions may be recorded; the Chair votes only in case of a tie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these procedural rules for Committee administration, meeting frequency, quorum, decision-making thresholds, and record-keeping of dissent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting and cost estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee shall submit an annual report to the Secretary of Commerce summarizing activity and recommendations to satisfy reporting requirements of OMB Circular A-119 and P.L. 104-113; the annual cost of operating the Committee is estimated (example: $31,000 including 0.20 staff year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an annual report that documents Committee activity and recommendations, and estimate and report operational costs as part of administrative transparency.
